title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Tanzania: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Tanzania: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Tanzania: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: Handling administrative, civil registration, probate, and benefit tasks after a death in the United Republic of Tanzania involves separate civil registration systems for Mainland Tanzania and Zanzibar, followed by court probate administration, social security benefit claims, tax clearance, and consular document legalization.

steps.title: Immediate Medical Confirmation and Mainland vs Zanzibar Death Registration
steps.html:
• Obtain an official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death from the attending health facility (or police/coroner report for non-hospital deaths) [1][2].
  • For deaths in Mainland Tanzania, register within 30 days under the Births and Deaths Registration Act (Cap. 108) with the Registration, Insolvency and Trusteeship Agency (RITA) via hospital wards or RITA district offices (and online via eRITA) to obtain an official Death Certificate [1][2].
  • For deaths in Zanzibar, register within 30 days under Zanzibar civil status legislation with the Zanzibar Civil Status Registration Agency (ZCSRA) by preparing applications through eCRVS and filing supporting documents at the nearest Unguja or Pemba ZCSRA office [3][4].

steps.title: Estate Probate, Wills, and Administrator-General Jurisdiction
steps.html:
• Identify whether a valid written or oral will exists (Registration, Insolvency and Trusteeship Agency (RITA) trusteeship guidance notes two witnesses with one clan and one non-clan witness for written wills, and four witnesses for oral wills) and check whether any will was deposited with RITA for safe custody [5][6].
  • Petition the Primary Court, District Court, or High Court under the Probate and Administration of Estates Act (Cap. 352) for a Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration, noting the statutory 90-day general citation period for objections, or request administration through the Administrator-General within RITA where applicable [5][12].

steps.title: Social Security Funeral Grants and Survivor Benefits
steps.html:
• File a Funeral Grant claim with the National Social Security Fund (NSSF) within 60 days of the member's death (with tiered lump sums depending on contribution history), and submit a Survivors' Pension claim for eligible dependants through NSSF [7][8].
  • For public-service contributors, file Survivors' Benefits claims (Form PS-BEN.2 and supporting civil certificates) with the Public Service Social Security Fund (PSSSF), where 180 or more monthly contributions qualify dependants for survivor pensions or lump sums under statutory rules [9].

steps.title: Tax Clearance and Financial Account Settlements
steps.html:
• Notify Tanzanian banks and insurers with certified copies of the Death Certificate, and await Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration before transferring accounts or real property titles [12].
  • Contact the Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA) to confirm final income tax status, Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) updates, and tax clearance certificates required prior to property transmission [10].

steps.title: Cross-Border Document Authentication (Non-Apostille)
steps.html:
• Tanzania is not a Contracting Party to the HCCH 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, so Apostille certificates do not replace consular legalization [13].
  • Certificates of death, Grants of Probate, and Letters of Administration intended for use abroad must be authenticated by the Legal Unit of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and East African Cooperation in Dodoma (or its department in Zanzibar) and subsequently legalized by the destination state's embassy [11].
